source.title: How GPT learns layer by layer
source.authors: Jason Du; Kelly Hong; Alishba Imran; Erfan Jahanparast; Mehdi Khfifi; Kaichun Qiao

record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE and probe feature analysis to OthelloGPT, a small GPT-based model, and reports which features the SAE recovers across layers. It does not reproduce or directly test superposition geometry from the original study.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE-based feature recovery and layer-wise measurements. It also compares SAE and linear-probe visualizations; no cited results from other work are recorded as this study's findings.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on OthelloGPT residual streams and reports single SAE features that classify tile color and tile stability (AUROC 0.80–0.95). That is a new-setting result on whether a dictionary recovers sparse, interpretable features in a trained transformer (V4). Its seed comparisons also bear weakly on V5. It does not examine toy-model geometry, capacity, polysemanticity causes or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that OthelloGPT layers encode different attributes (early layers board shape and edges, intermediate layers 2–4 stability, deeper layers dynamic changes), and that SAEs reveal more distinctive, disentangled features than linear probes. They acknowledge seed variability and possible compositional 'stability' features. The SAE-vs-probe superiority claim is qualitative, based on heatmaps, with no quantitative comparison.
record.recipe_differences: Analyzes SAE and linear-probe representations in OthelloGPT; does not use the original study's superposition toy-network setup or test its feature-geometry claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer and SAE initialization seed affect which tile-stability features are found; tile-color patterns are reported across 10 seeds, while stability analysis used two seeds.

fits_no_version.finding: The paper qualitatively compares SAEs with linear probes: probe accuracy rises over layers, and SAE heatmaps look more structured than probe–neuron cosine maps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features give more structured or disentangled layer-wise interpretations than linear probes in OthelloGPT. This is a method comparison, not a superposition claim.

record.code_released: not stated (the abstract says the code is publicly available via a GitHub Repository but gives no URL)
record.problems: Only one OthelloGPT testbed is described. Tile-stability analysis confirms results with two seeds and the authors report seed variability; feature interpretations are correlational, and the authors say causal perturbation and more seeds are needed. Several key visualizations are figures without extracted numerical values.
record.rows_left_out: The appendix reports additional individual feature-tile AUROC pairs in Tables 3–7 and feature activation counts across layers and seeds in Tables 1–2. They are not listed individually here; rows capture representative numerical results and the paper's stated layer-wise and seed-wise conclusions.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy models, geometry, sparsity transition or orthogonality measures.
All of it: no capacity or importance analysis of polysemantic neurons.

Untested: whether features are spread across many neurons (the neuron–probe cosine counts are in a figure only), and any LLM beyond OthelloGPT. Also untested: whether SAE features beat neuron or random baselines.
Completeness, canonicality, and a quantitative cross-seed feature-matching measure.

missing.what: Counts of MLP neurons with cosine similarity > 0.2 to each tile's 'my color' probe, per layer. This could bear on V4's 'spread across neurons' but is figure-only.

record.verdict_notes: OthelloGPT is a small game-trained transformer, not an LLM, so the V4 link is a stretch to a new setting. There are no controls (random features, neurons, untrained model) and no uncertainty estimates. Stability labels use a simplified rule. The Aizi (2024) 'SAEs find only 9/180 board state features' result is cited, not produced here, so it is not recorded.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular superposition geometry.
Does not test whether neurons are polysemantic because features compete for limited capacity.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
Tests SAE recovery of selected features in OthelloGPT, not whether real LLMs generally spread features across neurons or whether this generalizes beyond the Othello task.
Tests some cross-seed robustness of selected SAE features, but not completeness or canonicality of the dictionary features.
Does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: Othello-GPT
rows.stage_stated: trained on Synthetic Othello dataset; training stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Used SAE features from residual-stream embeddings to classify tile color; selected top features by AUROC across random seeds.

conditions.value: tile color (empty, player's piece, opponent's piece)

rows.measure: SAE feature AUROC and frequency of board positions among selected top features
rows.value: For each seed, selected the top 50 features with AUROC > 0.7; aggregated visualizations highlighted positions including edges and central tiles.
rows.note: The paper describes the position pattern as consistent across 10 seeds; exact per-position counts are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: The value mostly restates the selection procedure (top 50 features with AUROC > 0.7 per seed), not a measured result. The actual result, position frequencies, exists only as a heatmap (Fig. 3). There is no baseline such as random features, raw neurons or an untrained model. Keep the row, but read it as weak, figure-only evidence.

rows.note: One of the table's separately reported top feature-tile AUROC results.
rows.check: This value is the maximum of a selected top-k list (Table 3), so it is selected, not representative. No control AUROC (random direction or neuron) is given. r2–r7 are best cases and should be read as such.

rows.subject: Othello-GPT
rows.stage_stated: trained on Synthetic Othello dataset; training stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared layer-wise SAE feature activations with tile-stability labels; analyzed feature-activation frequencies with AUROC threshold > 0.8.

conditions.value: 104,000 board states (2,000 games x 52 board states per game)

rows.measure: Frequency of SAE feature activations associated with tile stability
rows.value: Authors report the highest frequency in layers 2 through 4; features 349 and 108 show a strong pattern.
rows.note: The paper says layers 1 and 5 through 8 do not appear to learn stability to the same extent, but may allocate capacity to other board-state aspects.
rows.check: The layer concentration (layers 2–4) describes where stability features appear. It does not qualify V4. Counts are in Tables 1–2 (e.g., feature 349 total 48, feature 108 total 47, seed 1). The 'seed 2' comparison may be a second OthelloGPT model rather than a second SAE seed: the Fig. 5 caption says 'another OthelloGPT model'.

rows.subject: Othello-GPT
rows.stage_stated: trained on Synthetic Othello dataset; training stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE feature findings across random initialization seeds and reported feature-activation counts across layers.
rows.measure: Consistency of SAE-discovered tile-color feature positions across seeds
rows.value: Authors report consistent identification of meaningful positions across 10 seeds, including edges and central tiles.
rows.note: This is evidence of some cross-seed consistency, not evidence that SAE features are complete or canonical.
rows.check: The heatmaps are aggregated across 10 seeds, so they cannot show per-seed consistency or feature matching. The 'robustness' claim is the authors' assertion, with no cross-seed feature-similarity measure. 'Partial' is not readable from the data.

rows.subject: Othello-GPT
rows.stage_stated: trained on Synthetic Othello dataset; training stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared tile-stability feature activations across two SAE seeds.
rows.measure: Cross-seed variability in selected stability-associated features and their layer distribution
rows.value: Authors report variability across seeds and note that interpreted stability features may be compositions of more granular features, such as edge or corner configurations.
rows.note: The authors say additional seeds and causal perturbations are needed to distinguish a stability feature from a composition of related features.
rows.check: Feature indices are arbitrary across SAE runs, so different IDs (349/108 vs 90/67/403) are not themselves evidence of instability. The paper gives no matching metric. The authors explicitly state seed variability and that 'stability' features may be compositions. The subject of 'seed 2' may be a different OthelloGPT model rather than a different SAE seed.

relationships.condition: OthelloGPT (8-layer, d=512) residual-stream SAEs, tile color and tile stability, seed 1
relationships.reason: Individual SAE features predict tile stability with AUROC up to 0.95 (layer 2), and tile-color features exceed 0.7 across seeds (r1–r8). These are selected top values with no control baseline, so support is weak.
relationships.display_finding: Individual SAE features predicted tile stability with AUROC up to 0.95 at layer 2, and tile-color features exceeded 0.7 across seeds. These are selected top values with no control baseline, so the evidence is weak.

relationships.condition: Tile-stability SAE features compared across two seeds/models
relationships.reason: Authors report variability across seeds and that 'stability' features may be compositions of more granular features (r10). There is no quantitative matching, and r9's aggregated heatmaps cannot show stability.
relationships.display_finding: The authors report variability across seeds and suggest the stability features may be compositions of more granular features, but give no quantitative matching.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: OthelloGPT SAE tile-color and stability feature analyses
reader_labels.reason: SAE features discriminate tile-color and stability labels; the paper reports top stability AUROCs above 0.8 and consistent tile-color patterns across seeds (r1–r8).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Tile-stability features across layers and seeds
reader_labels.reason: The stability signal is layer-dependent, concentrated in layers 2–4 by the authors' account, and varies across seeds; the study is limited to OthelloGPT (r8).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SAE feature robustness across initialization seeds
reader_labels.reason: Tile-color positions are described as consistent across 10 seeds, but stability features vary across two seeds and may comprise more granular features; completeness and canonicality are not established (r9–r10).
